overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the OML by refusing public comment during the Fire Chief complaint discussion, since the chair has discretion under G.L. c. 30A, § 20(f). The AG also noted the Board failed to respond to the complaint within 14 business days and reminded it to comply; no formal order was issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board refused to allow any public comment during a Sept. 29, 2010 open-session discussion of complaints against the Fire Chief.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair's decision not to allow public comment during the September 29, 2010 discussion of the complaint against the Fire Chief was, therefore, a proper exercise of his discretion under the law.

allegations.summary: The Board did not respond to the complaint filed with it on Oct. 5, 2010, as required within 14 business days under the OML complaint procedure.
allegations.key_passage: As a final matter, we note that the Board failed to respond to this Open Meeting Law complaint.
